name: Penicillium Mold
symptoms: Soft watery rot on fruits or plant tissues Blue-green or green powdery mold on infected areas Sunken lesions on fruit surfaces Rapid decay during storage Musty odor from infected produce
description: Penicillium is a genus of fungi commonly found in soil, air, and decaying organic matter. Many species cause post-harvest diseases in fruits and vegetables, producing blue or green molds and leading to significant storage losses.
management: Handle fruits carefully to avoid wounds Store produce at recommended temperature and humidity Remove infected fruits immediately Maintain clean storage facilities Use resistant varieties when available
prevention: Sanitize storage rooms and containers Avoid mechanical injury during harvest Proper ventilation in storage facilities Maintain cold chain for perishable crops
